title: The integral trick nobody teaches you
statement: Evaluate $$I = \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{dx}{1 + \tan^{2026} x}.$$ The exponent is deliberately absurd. You are not meant to antidifferentiate this.
solutionSteps: Try the reflection substitution $u = \tfrac{\pi}{2} - x$. The limits swap and come back around, so the interval is unchanged, and $du = -dx$ absorbs the flip.
Since $\tan\!\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2} - u\right) = \cot u$, the integral becomes $$I = \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{du}{1 + \cot^{2026} u}.$$ Same value, different-looking integrand.
Now add the two forms of $I$ together. With $t = \tan^{2026} x$, the integrands combine as $$\frac{1}{1 + t} + \frac{1}{1 + 1/t}.$$
Simplify that: $\dfrac{1}{1+t} + \dfrac{t}{t+1} = \dfrac{1 + t}{1 + t} = 1$. The exponent cancels itself out entirely.
Therefore $I = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ — and the $2026$ never mattered. Any positive exponent gives the same answer.
